name: Dharaneesh
bio: I'm a developer on a mission to turn ideas into reality through code. From building full-stack web apps with Next.js to crafting beautiful Linux desktops with Hyprland, I thrive on learning new technologies and solving real problems. Every mistake is a stepping stone to mastery, and every line of code is a chance to build something that matters.
philosophy: Everything you do, do it with care.

currently.title: The Little Things
currently.description: A fun little app that helps developers self-introspect about their workflow with guided prompts & personal AI insights. Built with React Native + Python backend.
currently.note: Stay tuned for the TestFlight release.

beliefs.title: Clean Code is a Conversation
beliefs.description: Code is read far more often than it's written. Every variable name, every function, every comment is a message to your future self and your teammates. Write code that tells a story.

beliefs.title: Build What Moves You
beliefs.description: The best work comes from genuine curiosity and passion. When you're building something that excites you, the late nights don't feel like work and the solutions come naturally.

beliefs.title: Your Tools, Your Rules
beliefs.description: Understanding your environment down to the config file gives you superpowers. Your OS should bend to your will, not the other way around. Linux taught me that.

whatILookFor.title: Impactful work
whatILookFor.description: Code that reaches real people and solves real problems. I want to build things that matter, not just features that ship.

whatILookFor.title: Meaningful challenges
whatILookFor.description: Hard problems that teach me something new. The best growth comes from the edge of your comfort zone.

whatILookFor.title: Great people to build with
whatILookFor.description: A team that cares about craft, communicates openly, and isn't afraid to say 'I don't know, let's figure it out together.'

aiDisclosure: This site was made by a human with real [ambitions, flaws, hopes, desires, late-night coding sessions, bad first drafts, good refactors, tab fatigue, debug victories, learning curves, curiosity, determination, caffeinated ideas, sleep-deprived epiphanies, and a genuine desire to make the web feel a little more human,] and with some assist from an A.I. collaborator to iterate ideas and check the copy.
mobileNote: This site is still finding its legs on mobile. I didn't want to just resize the desktop layout for smaller screens — it deserves its own thoughtful adaptation, and that's coming. In the meantime, please visit on desktop for the full experience. Otherwise, if your life needs a bit more chaos, feel free to scroll.
